text:
sasha: FYI incident on dedicated-pool-3: recurring OOMs over last 3 hours during long chat sessions (>12k tokens). GPU panic logs point at KV paging thrash + kernel fallback to safe-path. tail latency doubled and we saw ~20 503s from frontend. attaching quick notes. :frowning:
liam: ouch. can you paste the top lines from the gpu logs and runtime errs?
sasha: logs (snip):
```
E 03:12:01 gpu0 oom while allocating 4100000 bytes
W 03:12:01 kvpager: page-in loop detected for shard 4 (evictable=0)
I 03:12:02 kernel-selector: switched to fallback kernel (quant-safe) seq_len=12288
I 03:12:03 runtime: batching window forced flush size=1 due to memory pressure
```
more: pprof captured hot paths showing heavy pagewalker stalls on kv_lookup(). pprof command I ran: `pprof -http=:8080 /proc/self /tmp/heap.pb`
monitoring-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool-3 KV_PAGING_THROUGHPUT > 85% for 17m. SLA risk: latency_P95 breached by 2.1x.
natalie: timeline makes sense. long contexts are causing KV to hold many sticky slabs, fragmentation grows, then pager thrash when we try to compact. kernel flip is expensive too.
matt: any recent kernel-selection or batching rollouts? could a change have made the runtime pick a slower kernel earlier (reducing headroom)?
sasha: no large rollout in the last 24h. small opt landed in batching heuristics 3d ago but it was A/B. we need to check if traffic skew hit the A group.
liam: short triage checklist: 1) disable KV prefetch on that pool, 2) reduce max_request_seq_len for affected customer to 8k, 3) temporarily lower batch_max_tokens to avoid huge coalesced batches.
natalie: agree. additionally enable aggressive soft-evict (age-based) so we free sticky slabs sooner. that should reduce fragmentation while we investigate compaction regressions.
matt: propose quick config patch to dedicated-pool-3:
```
{"kv": {"prefetch": false, "soft_evict_age_ms": 60000, "max_cached_prefix_tokens": 8192},
 "batching": {"max_tokens": 4096, "max_concurrency": 6}}
```
can we push as a rollout to just that pool?
sasha: @deploy-bot can you do a one-off config rollout to pool id=dedicated-pool-3? use canary=1 and pause if error rate spikes.
deploy-bot: scheduled config rollout to dedicated-pool-3 (canary=1). will report back.
anika: long-term fixes to consider: 1) KV compaction background worker that coalesces adjacent free slabs, 2) telemetry to track per-shard sticky-slab ratio, 3) kernel-selection guard that avoids switching to fallback kernel until after a graceful drain attempt. we should also add a graceful degrade path: if kv memory > X% and paging rate high, route to small-ram model variant with stateless decoding.
liam: for immediate mitigation add an inline retry/backoff in front of requests that hit pagewalk stall: 1 quick retry with jitter and smaller batch preference. reduces chance of simultaneous heavy pagewalks.
natalie: testing note: repro locally with longctx-sim tool: `./longctx-sim --seq 14000 --users 30 --kv-hold=1` reproduces paging loop within ~2 minutes. I attached flame graphs to the ticket.
sasha: after rollout monitor: paging rate dropped from 88% -> 30% in the canary hosts. tail latency back to baseline on the canary. rolling to 25% of the pool now.
matt: :thumbsup: good. please open a follow-up RFC for the compaction worker + kernel guard and add an experiment row for 'soft_degrade_to_stateless' in the outage-runbook.
anika: logging todo: add a compactness metric and make it an alert rule (compactness < 0.6 for 5m). also surface kernel-switch events as traces in the request timeline.
sasha: agreed. creating issues: INF-8423 (compaction worker), INF-8424 (kernel guard), INF-8425 (observability for kernel-switches + compactness metric).
monitoring-bot: Incident update: canary rollout increased to 25% at 03:48:00. paging_throughput trending down.
liam: follow-up immediate hotfix: patch runtime to prefer prefix-evict instead of full-slab eviction when fragmented ratio > 0.7. simpler to implement and low-risk. anyone object?
matt: no objection. implement and small canary.
sasha: OK rolling hotfix to canary now. will monitor for new OOMs.
natalie: once hotfix is stable let's re-run longctx-sim with scale to verify we don't regress on latency. i'll own the test run.
liam: final note, we should update the SLA degrade playbook: when paging_throughput > 75% for 10m automatically enable soft-degrade routing to stateless-small and reduce concurrency for the pool. saves customer impact.
sasha: thanks all. will keep thread updated if we see more spikes. :eyes:
